title: Toyota Motor Corporation | History & Facts | Britannica Money
content: # Toyota Motor Corporation. **Toyota Motor Corporation**, Japanese parent company of the Toyota Group. In 1933 Toyoda Kiichiro founded what later became the Toyota Motor Corporation as a division of the Toyoda Automatic Loom Works, Ltd. In 1957 Toyota Motor Sales, U.S.A., Inc., was established, and the following year the company released the Toyopet sedan, its first model to be marketed in the United States; it was poorly received because of its high price and lack of horsepower. For several decades Toyota was Japan’s largest automobile manufacturer. The company took its present name in 1982, when Toyota Motor Company was merged with Toyota Motor Sales Company, Ltd. Two years later Toyota partnered with General Motors Corporation in the creation of New United Motor Manufacturing, Inc., a dual-brand manufacturing plant in California, where Toyota began U.S. production in 1986.

title: Toyota Motor Corporation | Business and Management | Research Starters | EBSCO Research
content: Toyota Motor Corporation (TMC), founded in 1937 and headquartered in Toyota City, Aichi, Japan, is a leading global automobile manufacturer known for its diverse range of vehicles, including cars, trucks, and hybrids. It became the world's largest automaker in 2008 and remains a significant player in the automotive industry, employing over 370,000 individuals and producing more than 200 million vehicles since its inception. Toyota is recognized for pioneering the hybrid vehicle market with the introduction of the Prius in 1997, which was the first mass-produced hybrid automobile. Toyota's impact extends beyond manufacturing; it plays a significant role in the global economy and has strategic partnerships, such as its collaboration with Mazda. title: History of Toyota | TOYOTA Motor Manufacturing UK
content: toyota-world-banner-range.jpg. # History of Toyota. Toyota's origins lie in the Japanese weaving industry when Sakichi Toyoda invented the world's first automatic loom and, subsequently, set up the Toyoda Spinning and Weaving Company in 1918. This in turn led to the launch of the Company's first ever passenger car in 1936, the Model AA, and in 1937, the Toyota Motor Company was born. Production of Toyota vehicles outside Japan began in 1959 in Brazil and now, besides its own plants, manufacturing subsidiaries and affiliates in Japan, Toyota manufactures Toyota and Lexus brand vehicles and components throughout the world. Look back at the history of Toyota, starting with the birth of founder Sakichi Toyoda. Find out more about the history of Toyota on the Toyota Motor Corporation website. title: History of Toyota | Trajectory of Toyota | Company | Toyota Motor Corporation Official Global Website
content: # History of Toyota. Ever since its founding, Toyota has pursued business activities centered on the production and sale of automobiles, with the aim of contributing to a more prosperous society. Here, we introduce Toyota's history from its founding to the present day. ## The Beginnings. Taking on the Automotive Business -Setting Course to Enter Automotive Business-. From 1937 -Establishment of Toyota Motor Co., Ltd.-. 1940s -Automobile Prototypes, Research and Development of Basic Technology-. 1950s -Business Management Crisis (Labor dispute); Establishment of Toyota Motor Sales Co., Ltd.-. ## Inheritance and Evolution. 1960s -Mass Production Systems Established; Development of Mass-market Vehicle-. 1970s -Satisfying Public Needs (Emissions standards, Oil crisis)-. 1980s -Sales and Manufacturing Operations Merged to Form Toyota Motor Corporation; Full-scale Overseas Production Launched-. 1990s -Response to Environmental and Safety Issues-. 2000s -Rapid Expansion of Globalization-.
